fixture_class: COURSE-OWNED SYNTHETIC REFERENCE SCENARIO — NOT LEARNER EVIDENCE
target_architecture: Synthetic local stateful service; learner must replace with actual project architecture

must_measure.target: Memory-growth behavior under the scenario workload
must_measure.methodology: Define a bounded workload and record actual memory observations on the target system
must_measure.success_criterion: Use the project-specific acceptance criterion recorded by the learner; no course-wide percentage is supplied
must_measure.criticality: A memory-growth fault could terminate a long-running process
must_measure.evidence_gap: No host-specific memory-growth observation is bundled with this synthetic fixture
must_measure.blast_radius_if_omitted: A release may ship without evidence about sustained-memory behavior

must_test.target: One project-specific security or data-integrity invariant
must_test.methodology: Run the actual course/project test that exercises the invariant and record the exact command/result
must_test.success_criterion: The chosen invariant-specific test must satisfy its explicit project contract
must_test.severity: Critical if the selected invariant protects authorization or durable data
must_test.criticality: Failure can cross a trust boundary or violate persistent-state correctness
must_test.evidence_gap: The synthetic fixture does not know which invariant or test exists in the learner project
must_test.blast_radius_if_omitted: A critical invariant could be unverified at release time

must_inspect.target: Deployment compatibility across application code and persisted schema/data
must_inspect.methodology: Inspect the actual candidate change, previous-version access patterns, and recovery evidence
must_inspect.success_criterion: Compatibility and recovery rationale are explicit and supported by project evidence
must_inspect.severity: High when a release changes persisted state
must_inspect.criticality: An incompatible rollback can make recovery slower or corrupt assumptions
must_inspect.evidence_gap: The bundled SQLite examples test only their own synthetic DDL/query pairs
must_inspect.blast_radius_if_omitted: Operators may discover code/data incompatibility only after a failed deployment

acceptable_unknown.description: A clearly bounded failure mode outside the current synthetic release scenario remains unmeasured
acceptable_unknown.justification: Acceptable Unknown is included to demonstrate honest scoping; the learner must replace this with a real project-specific uncertainty and reviewer-approved rationale
acceptable_unknown.criticality: Must be explicitly judged against the actual project scope
acceptable_unknown.evidence_gap: No evidence is collected for this out-of-scope condition
acceptable_unknown.blast_radius_if_omitted: The unknown could be forgotten rather than consciously accepted

deployment_compatibility.app_code_compatibility: Synthetic example: previous and candidate code compatibility must be established from actual API/data behavior; this fixture makes no project claim
deployment_compatibility.schema_compatibility_analysis: Synthetic example: a bundled SQLite DDL/query simulation may inform one compatibility question but does not prove whole-application rollback safety
deployment_compatibility.chosen_recovery_strategy: Project-specific recovery strategy to be selected only after compatibility and failure-mode analysis
deployment_compatibility.recovery_justification: This synthetic fixture demonstrates that the strategy needs an evidence-backed rationale; it does not prescribe rollback, roll-forward, reversal, snapshot, or canary as a universal answer
deployment_compatibility.stated_data_loss_bound: UNVERIFIED in this synthetic reference. The learner must derive any bound from the actual persistence configuration and failure model before reviewer PASS.
deployment_compatibility.reversal_verification_evidence: Synthetic reference only: run the bounded SQLite compatibility examples, then replace this with actual recovery evidence for the learner system
